title: Daily Devotional #39
paragraphs: As I reflect on Mark 11, I am struck by the power and authority that You displayed during Your earthly ministry. In this chapter, we see You entering Jerusalem triumphantly, riding on a donkey as the crowds shouted "Hosanna!" and laid their cloaks and palm branches on the road before You. This was a fulfillment of prophecy, as the prophet Zechariah had foretold that the Messiah would come in this way (Zechariah 9:9).

But Your actions didn't stop there. You went into the temple and drove out the merchants and money changers who were using it as a marketplace. You declared that the temple was to be a house of prayer for all nations, and that it had been turned into a den of robbers.

Lord, as I read this passage, I am convicted of the times when I have allowed distractions and worldly concerns to creep into my life and take up space that should be reserved for worship and prayer. I am reminded that You call us to live in a way that honors You in all aspects of our lives, and that includes how we approach our time in prayer and worship.

I am also reminded that You have the power to cleanse and purify. You didn't just drive out the merchants and money changers, You cleansed the temple of their influence. Lord, I pray that You would cleanse my heart and mind of any thoughts or desires that are not pleasing to You. Help me to focus on You and to seek Your will in all that I do.

Finally, I am struck by the power of faith. In this chapter, You curse a fig tree that has no fruit, and it withers and dies. Your disciples are amazed by this, and You tell them that if they have faith and do not doubt, they can move mountains.

Lord, I confess that my faith is not always as strong as it should be. But I pray that You would increase my faith, and that I would trust You more fully in all things. Help me to remember that nothing is impossible for You, and that with You all things are possible.
Thank You for Your power and authority, and for Your love and grace towards us. May we always honor You in all that we do, and may Your name be glorified in our lives.
In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
